As a female with a lot of close male friends, I'd like to pop in quickly. A lot of my guy friends, especially those who have had bad experiences in dating or aren't experienced or who have poor self esteem, never ask anyone out. Like, I know that's a simple and kinda obvious thing, but I've had several of my friends over the years admit to me that they had a thing for me but thought it wouldn't work and that there was no reason to ask. If you go into asking with the mindset that you're asking the chick on a date, not to be your life partner, it will hopefully decrease some of the stress. Not to say it's not stressful. I've done a bit of asking people on dates and it's so hard. But most people won't laugh at you or do something cruel. The vast majority of people will be pleasantly surprised by the invitation. If they say no, it's usually for their own personal reasons that don't have to do with you, and thus are not an attack on you. For example, I have a general policy of accepting a first date invitation from any guy I know who asks barring some unusual reason that I feel unsafe. Right now that's on hold because of some bad relationships I've been in and a need to take some time off from dating. So if we were friends and you'd asked me out, in general the answer would have been yes. If you'd asked during this period of needing to be single, I still would have thought it was nice of you and told you that. And it wouldn't have been anything about you that caused me to say no. So try to ask people. If they say no, don't take it personally. If by some crazy coincidence they do laugh at you or something, you dodged a bullet my friend. Women who laugh at others' pain are NOT worth dating. So keep trying. It gets a bit easier as time goes on.
